newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: SAIC to locate Latin America base in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: SAIC to locate Latin America base in Venezuela.

text.p: Science Applications International Corp (SAIC) will establish its Latin American base in Venezuela, John Glancy, SAIC executive vice-president said Thursday.

"We are basing here for three fundamental reasons: first is the strategic geographical location of the country, its technical and human resources and its active participation in regional trade agreements," Glancy told reporters at an oil conference in Caracas.
Employee-owned SAIC provides high technology products and services to government and private companies.

Officials at state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), the world's second largest oil company, revealed earlier Thursday that SAIC had been selected to run its internal information systems from 1997.
Glancy said SAIC's Latin America base would start operating in January.
According to SAIC figures Latin America's information market is worth $26 billion per year of which Brazil accounts for 48 percent, Mexico 21 percent and Venezuela 3.5 percent.
With annual revenues exceeding $2.2 billion, SAIC and its subsidiaries have 22,000 employees in more than 475 locations worldwide.
